summary: Issue #14 Footer redesign verified on desktop (/categories, 1440x900). All new testids present and correct: site-footer, 5 social pills (facebook/instagram/twitter/linkedin/youtube) with real https URLs and target=_blank, footer-contact-email as mailto:hello@baked.africa, footer-copyright with © 2026 BAKĒD text, footer-country with 🇨🇮 Côte d'Ivoire (desktop-only), footer-legal-links wrapper + 4 legal links (terms/privacy/cookies/accessibility) with correct hrefs. Brand promise text renders with Sparkles icon. Regression: all previously required footer-link-* testids (SHOP/FOOD/MART/AUTO seller/partner, blog, news, careers, help, partner, driver) still resolve. Legal link navigation to /terms works (200). Mobile stacking could NOT be verified — the context note said to visit /legal/terms or /legal/privacy 'which don't switch to MobileShell', but those routes do NOT exist in CustomerApp.jsx (only /terms and /privacy exist, both of which DO switch to MobileShell in mobile viewport, so Footer is not rendered).
action_items: Optional: add /legal/terms and /legal/privacy route aliases (or a LegalShell that always shows the site Footer regardless of viewport) so mobile Footer stacking is verifiable per the Issue #14 mobile acceptance criterion. Currently /terms and /privacy switch to MobileShell on 390px viewport, which hides the site Footer entirely. Not a Footer.jsx bug — a shell/route decision.
critical_code_review_comments: Footer.jsx (191 LOC) is clean, well-structured, uses env-independent constants — no issues.
LinkList testid derivation is deterministic (path -> footer-link-<slug>) which preserved existing Issue #12 testids across the refresh — good.
Country badge uses country?.flag && ... so falls back gracefully if context is missing.

success_rate.frontend: 97% (28/29 desktop checks passed; mobile stacking uncheckable due to missing /legal/* routes)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Footer Issue #14 fully verified on desktop. If retesting mobile, note that /terms and /privacy switch to MobileShell (bottom nav visible, site Footer hidden). Main agent needs to add a non-MobileShell legal route or a LegalShell wrapper that keeps the Footer visible on mobile.
